test_title: PYST 7: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 31 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Government of India Act 1935 proposed which major reform?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Establishment of federal government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** was a significant milestone in the constitutional history of India, proposing the establishment of an **All-India Federation**. This federation was intended to consist of **British Indian provinces** and **Princely States** as constituent units. Hence, the statement regarding the establishment of a federal government is correct.
 
• The Act introduced a clear division of powers between the **Centre** and the **Provinces** by categorizing subjects into three lists: the **Federal List** (59 items), the **Provincial List** (54 items), and the **Concurrent List** (36 items). **Residuary powers** were vested in the **Viceroy**.
 
• It abolished the system of **Dyarchy** in the provinces and introduced **Provincial Autonomy**, allowing provinces to act as autonomous units of administration. However, it simultaneously introduced **Dyarchy at the Centre** for federal subjects.
 
• The **Abolition of the Zamindari system** was not a part of this Act; it was a post-independence reform initiated through various state laws and the **1st Amendment** to the Constitution in **1951**. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
• The **Introduction of separate electorates** originally dates back to the **Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909**. While the 1935 Act extended this principle to **Scheduled Castes**, **women**, and **labor**, it was not the primary structural reform proposed. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
• The Act did not grant **Full independence** to India. It provided for limited self-governance while keeping the ultimate authority with the **British Parliament** and the **Viceroy**. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** was the longest Act passed by the **British Parliament** at that time, containing **321 sections** and **10 schedules**.
 
• It led to the establishment of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **1935** to regulate the currency and credit system of the country, following the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The Act provided for the creation of a **Federal Court**, which was inaugurated in **1937** in **Delhi**. This court served as the precursor to the modern **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• Under this Act, **Burma** (now **Myanmar**) was officially separated from **British India** in **1937**, and two new provinces, **Sindh** and **Orissa**, were created.
 
• The **franchise** (right to vote) was extended, granting approximately **10%** of the total population the right to vote, which was a significant increase from previous reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The proposed **All-India Federation** never actually came into existence because the **Princely States** refused to join it, fearing a loss of their internal sovereignty.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** served as the primary blueprint for the **Constitution of India** adopted in **1950**. Many features, such as the **federal scheme**, **office of the Governor**, **judiciary**, and **emergency powers**, were borrowed from this Act.
 
• The Act abolished the **Council of India**, which had been established by the **Act of 1858** to assist the **Secretary of State for India**.
 
• It also provided for the establishment of not only a **Federal Public Service Commission** but also **Provincial Public Service Commissions** and **Joint Public Service Commissions** for two or more provinces.
